content.title: Final Four odds: Expert picks to win March Madness
content.text: April 3, 2026, 6:05 a.m. ETFollowing a five-day layoff since the end of the Elite Eight, the 2026 Men's NCAA Tournament resumes action on Saturday, April 4, with the Final Four.The national semifinal double-header gets started at 6:09 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium, with No. 2 Connecticut vs. No. 3 Illinois. The heavyweight bout between No. 1 seeds Arizona and Michigan will tip off at approximately 8:49 p.m. ET.Both the Illini and Wolverines are looking to end the Big Ten's national championship drought that spans over a quarter-century. The Wildcats are also looking to end a lengthy national championship drought of their own, while the Huskies are looking to win their third title in the last four seasons.So, who is advancing to Monday's national championship from the Final Four and winning it all?Here's a look at the latest odds and USA TODAY Sports' expert picks:Final Four odds: Who is favored to win Men's NCAA Tournament?Odds courtesy of BetMGM as of Thursday, April 2Michigan (+165)Arizona (+185)Illinois (+425)UConn (+575)Michigan currently holds the best odds at winning the Men's NCAA Tournament on Monday night, according to BetMGM, with +165 odds.If the Wolverines can move past Arizona and win on Monday, it would mark the program's first national championship since 1989. It would also mark the first time a Big Ten program has won the Men's NCAA Tournament since 2000, when Michigan State won. Here's a breakdown of national championship odds among the Final Four teams:Experts pick Final Four teams to win national championship gameHere's a look at some of USA TODAY Sports' experts' picks to win the Men's NCAA Tournament:John Leuzzi: UConn — It's a toss-up for me between UConn and Arizona, but I side with the Huskies in this one. I trust Dan Hurley and UConn's experience in the national championship game (we saw this vs. Duke in the Elite Eight with the Huskies fight back from a near 20-point deficit). I also wonder how taxing the Michigan game will be on Arizona's bodies, and the quick turnaround/recovery from that. UConn will need to play a near perfect game, though.Jordan Mendoza: Arizona — The Wildcats are too deep and bully everyone on their path to a title.Ehsan Kassim: Illinois — Illinois might be the hottest team in the country and it'll win its first national title based on its offense and improved defense in the tournament.Austin Curtright: Arizona — Arizona is too efficient around the rim and at the free-throw line, and dominates teams in both facets. It also has multiple guards capable of shooting from outside, which makes it a dangerous team with virtually no weaknesses.The USA TODAY app gets you to the heart of the news — fast.
